holidays.name: Push Button Phone Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble push-button telephone. It's the day to remember when dialing meant a satisfying plastic click instead of a long, slow whirrrr. Press a few buttons, call someone you love, and enjoy how instant that tone-driven magic feels.
holidays.origin: The day marks the anniversary of the first commercial push-button telephone service, which Bell Telephone launched on November 18, 1963. Customers in Carnegie and Greensburg, Pennsylvania, were the first to try it. It replaced the rotary dial with the touch-tone system.
holidays.funFact: Touch-tone phones work by sending two tones at once for each button, one for the row and one for the column. This is called dual-tone multi-frequency signaling, or DTMF. It was much faster than waiting for a rotary dial to spin back.

holidays.name: Odd Socks Day
holidays.description: A day to ditch the matchy-matchy rule and wear two completely different socks on purpose. Stripes with polka dots, neon with argyle, a snowman with a taco: it all counts. The goal is to celebrate individuality and be proud of being a little mismatched.
holidays.origin: Odd Socks Day is an unofficial observance that has grown into a playful way to celebrate being different. Schools and groups often use it to promote kindness and to stand up to bullying. The idea is that you don't need to match to belong.
holidays.funFact: The mismatched-sock idea has become a symbol of embracing differences. Schools often hold odd-sock days with donation drives or anti-bullying messages, so one wardrobe quirk can carry a real message.
